questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the Revolt of 1857.
1. Rani Lakshmibai led the rebels at Jhansi.
2. Nana Sahib led the rebellion at Lucknow.
3. Kunwar Singh led the rebels in the Jagdishpur region of Bihar.
questions.explanation: Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi) and Kunwar Singh (Jagdishpur, Bihar) are correctly matched. Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal; Nana Sahib led at Kanpur.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Centres and leaders of 1857.
Option A (1 and 2 only) is out: Statement 2 is wrong: Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal; Nana Sahib led at Kanpur.
Option C (2 and 3 only) is out: Statement 2 is wrong and statement 1 is correct.
Option D (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 2 swaps the leaders of Kanpur and Lucknow.
Common slip to avoid: Swapping the Kanpur and Lucknow leaders.
So the answer is option B: 1 and 3 only.
questions.trap: Swapping the Kanpur and Lucknow leaders.
wrongReasons: Statement 2 is wrong: Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal; Nana Sahib led at Kanpur
Statement 2 is wrong and statement 1 is correct
Statement 2 swaps the leaders of Kanpur and Lucknow

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the Permanent Settlement of 1793.
1. It was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal and Bihar.
2. Zamindars were recognised as owners of land and paid a fixed revenue to the Company.
3. It was the first system introduced in the Madras and Bombay presidencies.
questions.explanation: Cornwallis fixed the revenue in perpetuity with the zamindars. Ryotwari (Munro, Read) was used in Madras and Bombay.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Permanent Settlement vs Ryotwari vs Mahalwari.
Option A (2 and 3 only) is out: Statement 1 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it.
Option B (1 and 3 only) is out: Statement 2 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it.
Option C (1, 2 and 3) is out: Madras and Bombay had the Ryotwari system, not the Permanent Settlement.
Common slip to avoid: Applying the zamindari system to south and west India.
So the answer is option D: 1 and 2 only.
questions.trap: Applying the zamindari system to south and west India.
questions.revise: Permanent Settlement vs Ryotwari vs Mahalwari
wrongReasons: Statement 1 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it
Statement 2 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it
Madras and Bombay had the Ryotwari system, not the Permanent Settlement

questions.text:
Match List I (Governor-General) with List II (Policy or event).
A. Lord Wellesley  B. Lord Dalhousie  C. Lord Curzon  D. Lord Ripon.
1. Doctrine of Lapse  2. Subsidiary Alliance  3. Partition of Bengal, 1905  4. Local self-government resolution, 1882
questions.explanation: Wellesley: Subsidiary Alliance; Dalhousie: Doctrine of Lapse; Curzon: Partition of Bengal (1905); Ripon: 1882 Local Self-Government resolution.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Governors-General and their policies.
Option A (A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4) is out: Wellesley and Dalhousie are swapped.
Option C (A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3) is out: Curzon and Ripon are swapped.
Option D (A-2, B-3, C-1, D-4) is out: Dalhousie is not linked with the Partition of Bengal.
Common slip to avoid: Swapping Wellesley and Dalhousie.
So the answer is option B: A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.
questions.trap: Swapping Wellesley and Dalhousie.
wrongReasons: Wellesley and Dalhousie are swapped
Curzon and Ripon are swapped

questions.text: The Uttaramerur inscriptions, which describe the working of village assemblies and the rules for electing their committees, belong to the reign of which Chola ruler?
questions.explanation: The Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I (c. 920 CE) detail the sabha and its committees, with eligibility rules and selection by lot.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Chola local self-government.
Option A (Rajaraja I) is out: He is known for the Brihadeeswara temple and a strong central administration.
Option B (Rajendra I) is out: He is known for naval expeditions to the Ganga and Southeast Asia.
Option C (Kulottunga I) is out: He belongs to the later Chola-Chalukya line.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Rajaraja I, the best-known Chola king.
So the answer is option D: Parantaka I.
questions.trap: Choosing Rajaraja I, the best-known Chola king.
wrongReasons: He is known for the Brihadeeswara temple and a strong central administration

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about amendment of the Constitution.
1. Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368, subject to the basic structure.
2. The basic structure doctrine was laid down in the Kesavananda Bharati case, 1973.
3. A Constitution Amendment Bill can be introduced only with the prior recommendation of the President.
questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) allows amendment of rights but not of the basic structure. Prior recommendation of the President is required for Money Bills, not for Constitution Amendment Bills.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Article 368, basic structure.
Option A (2 and 3 only) is out: Statement 1 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it.
Option B (1 and 3 only) is out: Statement 2 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it.
Option C (1, 2 and 3) is out: No prior presidential recommendation is needed to introduce an amendment Bill.
Common slip to avoid: Mixing the rule for Money Bills with amendment Bills.
So the answer is option D: 1 and 2 only.
questions.trap: Mixing the rule for Money Bills with amendment Bills.
wrongReasons: Statement 1 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it
Statement 2 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it
No prior presidential recommendation is needed to introduce an amendment Bill

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha.
1. Twelve members are nominated by the President.
2. Elected members are chosen by the single transferable vote under proportional representation.
3. It can be dissolved by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha has 12 nominated members and is elected by STV; it is never dissolved, one-third of its members retire every second year.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Composition of Parliament.
Option B (2 and 3 only) is out: Statement 1 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it.
Option C (1 and 3 only) is out: Statement 2 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it.
Option D (1, 2 and 3) is out: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution.
Common slip to avoid: Applying Lok Sabha dissolution to the Rajya Sabha.
So the answer is option A: 1 and 2 only.
questions.trap: Applying Lok Sabha dissolution to the Rajya Sabha.
wrongReasons: Statement 1 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it
Statement 2 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it
The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution

questions.text: Under which Article can Parliament legislate on a subject in the State List in the national interest if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by two-thirds of members present and voting?
questions.explanation: Article 249 empowers Parliament, after such a Rajya Sabha resolution, to make laws on State List matters for up to one year at a time.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Parliament's power over the State List: Arts 249, 250, 252, 253.
Option B (Article 250) is out: It applies during a proclamation of emergency.
Option C (Article 252) is out: It applies when two or more States request Parliament by resolution.
Option D (Article 253) is out: It applies to give effect to international treaties.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Article 250, the emergency provision.
So the answer is option A: Article 249.
questions.trap: Choosing Article 250, the emergency provision.
questions.revise: Parliament's power over the State List: Arts 249, 250, 252, 253
wrongReasons: It applies during a proclamation of emergency
It applies when two or more States request Parliament by resolution
It applies to give effect to international treaties

questions.text: The 16th Finance Commission, headed by Arvind Panagariya, is constituted under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, constituted every five years to recommend sharing of taxes and grants between the Union and the States.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Finance Commission: Article 280.
Option A (Article 275) is out: It deals with grants-in-aid to States.
Option B (Article 148) is out: It deals with the Comptroller and Auditor General.
Option C (Article 324) is out: It deals with the Election Commission.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Article 275 because it mentions grants.
So the answer is option D: Article 280.
questions.trap: Choosing Article 275 because it mentions grants.
wrongReasons: It deals with grants-in-aid to States
It deals with the Comptroller and Auditor General

Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax.
1. The GST Council is established under Article 279A.
2. The Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson of the GST Council.

So the answer is option A: 1 and 2 only.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
1. CRR must be maintained by banks as cash balances with the RBI.
2. SLR may be maintained in liquid assets such as cash, gold and government securities.
3. Banks earn interest from the RBI on the CRR balances.
questions.explanation: CRR is held with the RBI and earns no interest; SLR is held by the bank itself in liquid assets.
steps: Spot what the question tests: CRR vs SLR.
Option A (2 and 3 only) is out: Statement 1 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it.
Option B (1 and 3 only) is out: Statement 2 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it.
Option C (1, 2 and 3) is out: The RBI pays no interest on CRR balances.
Common slip to avoid: Thinking CRR deposits earn interest.
So the answer is option D: 1 and 2 only.
questions.trap: Thinking CRR deposits earn interest.
wrongReasons: Statement 1 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it
Statement 2 is correct, so this option wrongly drops it
The RBI pays no interest on CRR balances

questions.text: In a hypothetical budget, total expenditure is Rs 48.0 lakh crore, total receipts excluding borrowings are Rs 33.0 lakh crore and interest payments are Rs 11.0 lakh crore. What is the primary deficit?
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = 48.0 - 33.0 = 15.0. Primary deficit = fiscal deficit - interest = 15.0 - 11.0 = 4.0 lakh crore.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit - interest.
Option A (Rs 15.0 lakh crore) is out: This is the fiscal deficit, before interest is deducted.
Option C (Rs 11.0 lakh crore) is out: This is the interest bill, not the deficit.
Option D (Rs 26.0 lakh crore) is out: Interest has been added instead of subtracted.
Common slip to avoid: Stopping at the fiscal deficit.
So the answer is option B: Rs 4.0 lakh crore.
questions.trap: Stopping at the fiscal deficit.
wrongReasons: This is the fiscal deficit, before interest is deducted
This is the interest bill, not the deficit
Interest has been added instead of subtracted

questions.text: Which committee recommended that India adopt flexible inflation targeting and set up a Monetary Policy Committee?
questions.explanation: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended the monetary policy framework; the MPC was formed in 2016.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Committees: Urjit Patel, Narasimham.
Option A (Rangarajan Committee) is out: It dealt mainly with poverty estimation and balance of payments.
Option B (Narasimham Committee) is out: It recommended banking sector reforms.
Option D (Y. V. Reddy Committee) is out: It is not linked with inflation targeting.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the Narasimham Committee.
So the answer is option C: Urjit Patel Committee.
questions.trap: Choosing the Narasimham Committee.
wrongReasons: It dealt mainly with poverty estimation and balance of payments
It recommended banking sector reforms
It is not linked with inflation targeting

2. Neeraj Chopra won silver in javelin at Paris 2024.

So the answer is option A: 1 and 2 only.

So the answer is option B: 1 and 2 only.

questions.text: The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol aims to phase down which group of substances?
questions.explanation: The 2016 Kigali Amendment targets HFCs, which do not harm ozone but are strong greenhouse gases.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment.
Option A (Chlorofluorocarbons) is out: Phased out under the original Montreal Protocol.
Options B and D are out: Not covered by the amendment.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing CFCs, the original target of the Protocol.
So the answer is option C: Hydrofluorocarbons.
questions.trap: Choosing CFCs, the original target of the Protocol.
